data.gender_notes: Prue is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Middle English word 'pruet', meaning 'to try'. The name Prue was used in the 17th century as a diminutive of the name Philippa, which means 'lover of horses'. In the Bible, there is a character named Prue, who is one of the three sisters mentioned in the book of Ruth. The name Prue carries the meaning “Trust” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Prue usually hope their child will grow to embody trust and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and trust in the divine.
data.etymology: Prue belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Trust.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Prue total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
